title: Config Drift Sentinel: telemetry-gated rollback, staged checkpoints, and KV-state harmonization
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Problem: Configuration changes that touch batching, caching, and routing frequently cause subtle cost or latency regressions that only become evident under real traffic patterns, or they corrupt runtime KV cache coherency leading to silent correctness issues. Current manual rollback is slow and unsafe for stateful changes. Goal: Implement an automated "Config Drift Sentinel" that combines telemetry gating, staged checkpoints, and state reconciliation to safely apply or automatically roll back config changes related to batching and caching.
acceptance_criteria: Config changes that match batching/cache change templates can be applied behind a telemetry gate
If latency or token-cost delta exceeds configured thresholds within the canary window, the system automatically triggers a staged rollback and quarantines KV prefix changes
Rollbacks are reversible and produce an audit artifact (checkpoint id + diff) that allows postmortem replay
End-to-end test harness reproduces a synthetic cost/latency regression and verifies automated rollback completes within SLA
All actions are surfaced in Console with clear reason, thresholds, and links to artifacts
proposed_implementation: 1) Preflight: static linter for batching/caching config keys + simulated dry-run in a lightweight sandbox (small model/trace). 2) Apply: create a sequential checkpoint (immutable snapshot id) before applying and stage change as 'shadow-apply' to x% traffic for canary. 3) Telemetry gate: collect signals for canary window (latency p95, per-token cost, error-rate, KV-miss-rate). 4) Decision logic: evaluate thresholds + trend detection (regression > 15% cost OR latency p95 increase > 30% OR KV-miss spike). 5) Automatic response: (a) if transient, expand canary; (b) if regression persistent, trigger staged rollback: stop routing new shadow requests, replay safe rollback plan that restores checkpoint, and quarantine affected KV prefixes using tombstone marker. 6) Reconciliation: run state harmonizer that replays idempotent operations for affected requests and reconciles KV cache shards. 7) Post-action: attach telemetry snapshot, candidate diffs, runbook link and open tagged incident in tracking system.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal-only feature flag for infra teams, enable preflight lint and checkpoint creation for all config applies. Phase 2: pilot with batching/cache teams (two services) using 5% shadow traffic for 2 weeks. Phase 3: enable auto-rollbacks for P1 regressions and expand to select customers. Phase 4: GA with default conservative thresholds and Console controls for tuning.
runbook: Trigger: telemetry gate fires or operator manually aborts. 1) Confirm alert and open incident. 2) Inspect checkpoint id and config diff in Console. 3) If auto-rollback in progress, monitor job completion and verify restored checkpoint state. 4) Run KV-harmonizer diagnostic (dry-run) to estimate unresolved consistency. 5) If reconciliation fails, escalate to runtime-safety on-call and disable automated applies until root cause addressed. 6) Post-incident: attach causal analysis, adjust thresholds or lint rules, and schedule follow-up changes.
test_plan: Unit tests for lint rules and decision logic, integration tests that simulate canary traces with injected latency/cost regressions, chaos tests that simulate KV shard partition during apply, and e2e staging run with synthetic customer traffic verifying rollback time and data consistency. Also backfill telemetry baselines for relevant routes to calibrate thresholds.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives cause unnecessary rollbacks -> Mitigation: add hysteresis, require 2 consecutive windows before full rollback
Risk: quarantine leaves stale tombstones causing tail latency -> Mitigation: TTL-based tombstones and reconciliation sweeper
Risk: checkpoint restore time may breach SLA on hot shards -> Mitigation: incremental snapshot + pre-warm path for hot prefixes
Risk: complexity increases operational burden -> Mitigation: provide Console UI with one-click abort/force-apply and clear diagnostics
